issues.problem: Says uniform convergence 'lets limits pass through integrals' without restriction; the lesson's own pitfall ((1/n)e^{-x/n} on [0,∞)) shows this fails on unbounded intervals.
issues.fix: Restricted to 'integrals over bounded intervals'.

issues.where: example: Summing a series by integrating term by term
issues.problem: Said 'the missing step is Abel's theorem' for 1 - 1/2 + 1/3 - ... = ln 2, implying uniform convergence/Abel is needed. In fact the error can be integrated directly (≤ 1/(n+2)); uniform convergence is sufficient, not necessary. Cross-reference to Abel's theorem in [[power-series]] checked: that lesson states it (without proof) and derives ln 2 from it, so the link is accurate.
issues.fix: Added the two-line direct estimate |ln 2 - S| = ∫_0^1 t^{n+1}/(1+t) dt ≤ 1/(n+2) and kept Abel's theorem as the general tool; added a check.

issues.problem: 'Converges uniformly on every closed interval strictly inside its interval of convergence' is vague.
issues.fix: Stated as: a power series with radius R converges uniformly on [-r, r] for every 0 < r < R.

issues.problem: Last bullet (order of quantifiers) repeats the intro and definitions.
issues.fix: Removed; minor trims in intro and first proof; minutes 21 → 20.

issues.problem: Reduction to 'everywhere' was incomplete: it did not say the exceptional set is a countable union of null sets, nor handle g = ∞ on a null set (needed so that g ± f_n are defined and ∫g can be cancelled), nor note f_n integrable; liminf/limsup sign step unstated.
issues.fix: Rewrote: defines the exceptional set N (non-convergence, |f_n| > g for some n, g = ∞), shows it is null, redefines all functions as 0 on N, notes f, f_n integrable, invokes linearity, and states liminf(-a_n) = -limsup a_n.

issues.where: theorem: Monotone convergence and Fatou's lemma
issues.problem: Hypotheses slightly loose: value range [0, ∞] not stated; measurability of the limit f and of liminf f_n not mentioned.
issues.fix: Stated for measurable f_n with values in [0, ∞] on (X, F, μ); added that f and liminf f_n are measurable.

issues.problem: 'MCT comes almost directly from the definition' understates the proof (it needs countable additivity); Fatou's derivation only gestured at.
issues.fix: Said what the MCT proof uses (sup over simple functions + countable additivity, Folland Ch. 2) and gave the complete short proof of Fatou from MCT via g_n = inf_{k≥n} f_k.

issues.problem: 'Null' and 'almost everywhere' were defined only for Lebesgue outer measure but used for a general measure μ in the DCT.
issues.fix: Added: a null set is a set in F of measure 0; a.e. means outside some null set.

issues.problem: Countable subadditivity proof covers A_k with length ≤ m*(A_k) + ε/2^k, which is meaningless when some m*(A_k) = ∞.
issues.fix: Added 'if the right side is finite' (otherwise trivial).

issues.where: example: Dominated convergence at work (Gauss product)
issues.problem: Gamma step did not state the dominating function's integrability (needs s > 0), did not say how the closed form arises, nor state the formula being proved.
issues.fix: Added 0 ≤ f_n x^{s-1} ≤ e^{-x}x^{s-1}, integrable since s > 0; 'integrating by parts n times'; displayed Γ(s) = lim n! n^s/(s(s+1)…(s+n)) for s > 0. Verified the integral identity symbolically and the limit numerically (new check).

issues.problem: 'Every set obtained from intervals by countably many unions, intersections and complements is measurable' misdescribes the Borel sets (the σ-algebra needs transfinite iteration, not 'countably many operations').
issues.fix: Replaced by 'every Borel set (a set in the smallest σ-algebra containing the intervals)'.

issues.where: example: An uncountable null set / pitfall / connection
issues.problem: 'No digit 7' example verified correct (9^k intervals of length 10^-k; 0/1-digit strings give distinct numbers; uncountable, null). Pitfall bullet 'null does not mean countable' duplicated it; Gamma mention duplicated in connection.
issues.fix: Moved the 'null ≠ countable' remark into the example, removed the duplicate bullet and duplicate Gamma mention; added a check on distinct 0/1 decimals and on exercise 3's dominating function.

issues.problem: DCT key statement omitted measurability of f_n.
issues.fix: Added 'f_n measurable'.

issues.problem: Over-long for a school lesson (author's count ~2,700 raw words); padding in intro, geometric aside, Gauss–Jordan paragraph, row-operation definition, examples' closing remarks, pitfalls and connection (factoring algorithms, combinatorics methods are beyond a 15-year-old's prerequisites).
issues.fix: Trimmed throughout to ~1,570 words of prose (excluding math); connection shortened to matrices/vector spaces/determinants/finite fields; pitfalls merged from 5 to 4 bullets; four-cycle discussion compressed; minutes 25 → 20.
